narrative.overview: Warm ivory stationery, burgundy ink, old-rose botanicals, fine arch rules, and expressive names create a personal romantic invitation. The continuous page alternates light paper passages with dark wine ceremony and closing passages; the guest first opens the burgundy lace envelope copied from Ryan & Anne’s implementation.
keyCharacteristics: Calligraphic names paired with editorial serif headings and readable prose.
Generated raster roses and a textured wax seal, paired with the couple’s supplied monogram artwork.
Spacious centered compositions, fine rules, and restrained one-time reveals.
Five alternating photo-and-text story chapters, with one supplied photograph per chapter.

rules.name: The Type Roles Rule
rules.body: Keep script for names and brief personal expressions; keep essential details and form instructions in the readable serif or sans-serif roles.

dos: Do keep client styling and artwork scoped to this invitation.
Do preserve the four distinct typography roles.
Do keep the main content visually hidden and inert until the cover handoff completes.
Do use responsive static-import artwork with decorative empty alternatives and unobstructed text.
Do retain focus visibility, native form semantics, and reduced-motion handling.
donts: Don't replace the real rose and wax-seal artwork with emoji or CSS approximations.
Don't use script for paragraphs, fields, or essential logistics.
Don't present the local reply preview as a saved RSVP.
Don't copy this client's palette or ornament into shared styles.
